# A rational barycentric transport for unequal three-fiber masses

This note constructs an exact halfspace domination, beyond the basic
centroid-leaf midpoint certificate, for the interval fibers

    A=[-2,2], B=[-5/4,11/4], D=[-1/2,1/2]

at integer coordinates -1,0,1. Their masses are 4,4,1. All maps and weights
below are rational. The construction also tensors with any common convex
continuous factor and therefore handles the d=3 midpoint-tree limitation
example in additive-midpoint-tree-limitation.md.

## Source-usage lemma

Suppose a finite collection of positive measures parametrizes singleton
outputs or pair outputs in a convex body C. Each singleton output equals
its one source. Each pair output is the midpoint of its two sources, and
all outputs belong to one chosen integer fiber. Let rho be the sum of the
output measures, and suppose the sum of ALL source marginals, counting two
sources for each pair, is bounded above by the mixed-integer measure mu_0
as measures. Then for every closed ambient halfspace H,

    rho(H)<=mu_0(H).                               (S)

Indeed a singleton in H has its source in H. A midpoint in H has at least
one source in H: the complement of a closed halfspace is convex. Thus
1_H(output)<=sum_sources 1_H(source) pointwise. Integrate and use the
source-marginal domination. This controls oblique halfspaces and retains
all boundary mass. No probabilistic selection of the final center occurs.

## Exact target and source budget

Let mu_0 be unnormalized mixed measure on the three interval fibers above,
of total mass 9. We will produce rho of total mass 9/2 uniformly on

    {0} x J,  J=[-5/4,9/4],

with continuous density 9/7. Consequently the corresponding target
probability measure nu satisfies nu(H)<=2 mu(H) for every ambient closed
halfspace, where mu=mu_0/9.

There are three sorts of outputs: outer endpoint pairs, central pairs,
and central singletons. The outer pairs have mass 1; the central pairs
have mass 1/2; the singletons have mass 3.

## Outer endpoint pairs

Let f be the following probability density on [-5/4,5/4]:

    2/7     on [-5/4,-3/4],
    9/28    on [-3/4,-1/4],
    67/140  on [-1/4,1],
    11/28   on [1,5/4].

Its respective interval masses are 1/7, 9/56, 67/112, 11/112, summing to
one. Let T(q), 0<=q<=1, be its continuous increasing quantile function:

    -5/4+(7/2)q                       if 0<=q<=1/7,
    -3/4+(28/9)(q-1/7)                if 1/7<=q<=17/56,
    -1/4+(140/67)(q-17/56)            if 17/56<=q<=101/112,
    1+(28/11)(q-101/112)              if 101/112<=q<=1.

For Lebesgue measure dq pair the two sources

    (-1,L(q)), (1,R(q)),
    R(q)=q-1/2, L(q)=2T(q)-R(q).

Their midpoint is (0,T(q)), with output density f. R pushes dq to ordinary
Lebesgue measure on D. L is continuous and strictly increasing from -2
to 2. Its four successive derivatives are

    6, 47/9, 213/67, 45/11,

all at least one. Hence its source marginal has density at most one on A.
It consumes exactly one unit of the available four units in that fiber.

## Central pairs

For 0<=s<=1/2, with measure (11/14) ds, pair

    X_1(s)=-1/4+5s, Y(s)=11/4-s,

both in fiber zero. Their midpoint is 5/4+2s. This contributes output
density 11/28 on [5/4,9/4]. For the same parameter interval with measure
(3/14) ds, pair

    X_2(s)=-3/4+6s, Y(s)=11/4-s.

Their midpoint is 1+(5/2)s. This contributes output density 3/35 on
[1,9/4]. The combined central-pair output mass is 1/2.

The two Y source marginals together are exactly Lebesgue measure on
[9/4,11/4]. The combined X source marginal has density

    1/28    on [-3/4,-1/4],
    27/140  on [-1/4,9/4].

These statements follow by the constant derivatives of X_1, X_2, Y;
in particular (11/14)/5+(3/14)/6=27/140.

## Central singletons

Use the remaining central source measure below 9/4 as singleton outputs:

    1        on [-5/4,-3/4],
    27/28    on [-3/4,-1/4],
    113/140  on [-1/4,9/4].

Its mass is 3. Together these singletons and both source marginals of
the central pairs use exactly the original Lebesgue measure on B.

## Verification of the uniform output

The combined output densities, listing outer / singleton / central-pair
contributions, are:

| Interval | Outer | Singleton | Central pairs | Sum |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [-5/4,-3/4] | 2/7 | 1 | 0 | 9/7 |
| [-3/4,-1/4] | 9/28 | 27/28 | 0 | 9/7 |
| [-1/4,1] | 67/140 | 113/140 | 0 | 9/7 |
| [1,5/4] | 11/28 | 113/140 | 3/35 | 9/7 |
| [5/4,9/4] | 0 | 113/140 | 11/28+3/35 | 9/7 |

There is no output outside J. Thus rho has total mass (9/7)(7/2)=9/2.
The source-usage lemma now proves the asserted uniform-target domination.
All sources lie in the prescribed fibers and every pair's midpoint is
in fiber zero. Convexity is respected; in this explicit example the
midpoint interval of A,D is contained in B.

## Tensoring with a convex factor and the resulting center

Let K be any compact convex body in R^r with positive r-volume; for r=0
use the single zero-dimensional point. Replace every fiber interval I
by I x K. In every singleton or pair construction above, draw an
independent k uniformly from K and use the SAME k coordinate for all
sources in that output. The target continuous coordinate is then (t,k).
Multiply all measures above by vol_r(K). Each source bound and the
uniform target identity tensor exactly with volume on K. The resulting
probability target is uniform on the (r+1)-dimensional body J x K, and

    nu(H)<=2 mu(H)

still holds for every closed halfspace in R x R^{r+1}, including normals
coupling all its coordinates. The centroid of J x K is

    (1/2,g_K).

Grunbaum's ordinary inequality at this single point gives

    depth_mu(0,1/2,g_K)>=gamma_{r+1}/2.

For the contributor's r=2 simplex example this proves the exact required d=3
constant at a point distinct from the middle-fiber centroid (whose
interval coordinate is 3/4) and from the endpoint-centroid midpoint
(whose interval coordinate is zero).

This is one exact construction and a reusable sufficient source-usage
criterion. It is not a claim that such a uniform target or allocation
exists for every convex three-fiber family.
